newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE sugar down, trade directionless.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE sugar down, trade directionless.

text.p: LIFFE sugar eased in quiet directionless trade.
May was most active, with 222 of 261 lots traded by 1700 GMT. It was $1.50 lower at $308.50.
"It isn't very exciting," one said. "Sentiment is slightly bearish, and some people are pricing above the market," he said.
"People are waiting for the funds to bail them out," he said.
He didn't reckon that the market was weak enough to inspire a barrage of fund selling.
None of the fundamental news was enough to get London moving.
The USDA forecast a 1996/97 sugar stocks-to-use ratio of 14.0 percent. This means that the import quota automatically goes up by 200,000 tonnes.
Peru's sugar cane production fell in January by 4.7 percent to 525,486 tonnes compared to the same month last year, the Agriculture Ministry said Tuesday.
The Indian government has released 2.25 million tonnes of sugar for domestic free sale in April, May and June, a Food Ministry statement said on Tuesday.
"The quota for April is 700,000 tonnes, for May it is 750,000 tonnes and for June it is 800,000 tonnes," the statement said.
